waiver_targets.name: T.J. Hockenson
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
T.J. Hockenson sustained a concussion in Week 5, so you'll want to check his status before bidding on him. But chances are he'll be ready to go in Week 7 when the Vikings come out of their bye week.

Hockenson has an appealing Week 7 matchup against the Colts, who entered Week 6 having given up the 10th-most fantasy points to tight ends. In Week 8, Hockenson gets an even better matchup against the Lions, who have allowed far and away the most fantasy points to TEs this year.

If you're streaming tight ends, Hockenson should be able to more than adequately cover you at the position for the next two weeks.

waiver_targets.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
In his first NFL game, Omar Cooper Jr. played just five offensive snaps and had a 30-yard catch on his only target before sustaining a high-ankle sprain that landed him on IR.

Cooper came off IR in Week 6 and had 6-103-1 on seven targets. His touchdown came on a 48-yard bomb. Cooper also had another touchdown negated by a dubious offensive pass interference penalty called against Jets WR Tim Patrick.

The 30th overall pick in this year's draft, Cooper is a hard-nosed gamer who has good hands and is dangerous after the catch. He can also line up either outside or inside. (Cooper played in the slot on Sunday when the Jets used three-receiver sets.)

Cooper probably isn't going to challenge Garrett Wilson's alpha receiver status on the Jets anytime soon, but he can be an effective No. 2 or No. 3.

Although the Jets will probably be getting Adonai Mitchell back from a finger injury in a week or two, Cooper could be a solution for WR-needy fantasy teams. He has playable matchups against the Dolphins and Raiders the next two weeks.

waiver_targets.name: Mike Washington Jr.
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note: Ashton Jeanty has been banged up all season. If Jeanty were to miss any time, rookie Mike Washington Jr. would assume a big workload for Las Vegas. A fourth-round pick out of Arkansas, the 6-1, 223-pound Washington is a size-speed freak who clocked a 4.33 at the scouting combine.

waiver_targets.name: Michael Mayer
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
The Raiders' passing attack is unconventional in that the team's No. 2 tight end is more fantasy-relevant than the No. 2 wide receiver.

Brock Bowers is not only the Raiders' No. 1 tight end, but the No. 1 tight end in the entire NFL. To Michael Mayer's credit, he's managing to thrive in Bowers' shadow. Mayer actually outproduced Bowers in Week 6, with 7-95-0 on nine targets against the Bills. Bowers had 4-70-0 on nine targets.

Mayer is averaging 5.7 targets, 4.7 catches and 44.7 receiving yards per game. He's playable in a pinch this week and can be a solid backup tight end in leagues where rostering more than one TE makes sense.

waiver_targets.name: Terrance Ferguson
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note: Terrance Ferguson is on IR with an ankle injury but is eligible to come off in Week 8. Ferguson flashed his plus athleticism with 6-54-1 on nine targets against the Giants in Week 2. He could be prominently involved in the Rams' passing game upon his return, particularly if WR Davante Adams misses time with the knee injury he sustained in Week 6.

waiver_targets.name: Jaylen Wright
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note: Ollie Gordon has seized command of Miami's lead-back role, but we shouldn't completely dismiss the possibility that Jaylen Wright plays a fantasy-relevant role at some point. Last season, it was often hard to discern whether Gordon or Wright was the top backup to De'Von Achane. It's clear that Gordon is ahead of Wright on the depth chart now, but it's worth keeping the speedy Wright on the radar and perhaps claiming him if you have a roster spot to spare.

waiver_targets.name: Cleveland Browns
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
Since Week 2, the Browns have held opponents to 17.6 points a game. This week, they face the Titans, who are averaging 14.0 points and 236.3 yards of offense per game.

The Titans are a great target for streaming defenses, and the Cleveland D has become respectable.

waiver_targets.name: Michael Penix Jr.
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
In a week where palatable streaming QB options are limited, Michael Penix Jr. is a solid option.

Penix has thrown for at least 223 yards in all four of his starts this season. After throwing a single TD pass in each of his first three games, he threw for three touchdowns vs. the Bears in Week 6.

Although he's averaging a modest 16.4 fantasy points per start, Penix has been efficient, averaging 8.6 yards per pass attempt. The Falcons are never going to be pass-heavy when they have Bijan Robinson in the backfield, so Penix needs to be efficient to have any fantasy value.

Penix has a tricky matchup this week against a 49ers defense that has given up 6.1 yards per pass attempt and has allowed five TD passes over its first five games. But the 49ers also have the sort of high-powered offense that could force the Falcons into a shootout and pump up the pass volume for Penix.

You could also use Penix against a pass-funnel Buccaneers defense in Week 8 and against the Bengals in Week 9.

waiver_targets.name: Geno Smith
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
Geno Smith can be an effective quarterback if he has time to throw, and this week he faces a Miami defense that has recorded four sacks in five games and has generated a pressure rate of 18.4% — among the lowest in the league. The Dolphins also have an opponent passer rating of 115.0 — among the highest in the league.

Smith added another weapon to his arsenal in Week 6, with rookie Omar Cooper coming back from an ankle injury on Sunday and catching six passes for 103 yards and a touchdown.

Smith is a solid matchup-based streamer for Week 6.

waiver_targets.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
Ryan Fitzgerald is 11-of-11 on field goals this season. He was 2-of-2 Sunday in Philadelphia, with one of his FGs coming from 52 yards. Fitzgerald had had trouble with extra points, however — he missed his fourth one of the season on Sunday and is 11-of-15 on PATs.

Fitzgerald is averaging 10.4 fantasy points per game. He has a Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers, who have allowed the most fantasy points to kickers this season.

waiver_targets.name: Evan McPherson
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
Evan McPherson is perfect on the season, having gone 10-for-10 on field goals and 14-of-14 on extra points. He's averaging 10.8 fantasy points per game.

The Bengals have one of the more potent offenses in the league and are averaging 25.6 points per game, giving McPherson a sturdy floor.

waiver_targets.name: Adonai Mitchell
waiver_targets.fp_waiver_note:
Adonai Mitchell showed a spark early this season with 3-60-0 against the Titans in Week 1 and 6-63-0 on 12 targets against the Packers in Week 2, but a finger injury has kept Mitchell sidelined for the last four weeks.

Mitchell is likely to be back either this week or next. His impending return might have been more eagerly anticipated by waiver shoppers were it not for a dazzling Week 6 performance by rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr., who came off IR and had 6-103-1 on seven targets against the Patriots.

Mitchell might be worth a speculative addition, but keep the FAAB bids small.
